reason: This passage from Exodus 2:11-15 depicts Moses witnessing the oppression of his Hebrew kinfolk and taking independent action to help them, but it contains no reference to God (Yahweh) or religious devotion. The Hebrews are presented as an enslaved people suffering burdens (סִבְלֹתָם), and Moses acts on his own initiative—before his actual call by God at the burning bush. The passage focuses on Moses's violent intervention, his concealment of the Egyptian, and his subsequent flight to Midian, rather than demonstrating the Hebrews as 'first and foremost followers of Yahweh.' The statement is not supported by the explicit content of this text.
